works.textChainNote: The Russian lyric follows Rutgers's seven-stanza Zelfverloochening, Evangelische Gezangen (1806), hymn 68. It is not a verbatim translation of the complete Lodenstein poem.
works.dateClaimNote: 4 January 1674 is supported by the 1727 edition and by both modern editions, and by the December 1673 hostage context of the Rees group. The 1676 impression is reported to misprint 1664. Only the literal reading of the 1676 leaf remains unresolved.
openChecks: Do not conflate I. Hert-sterckte in Jehova (printed pp. 78-81, 28 December 1673) with II. Hert-sterckte (printed pp. 82-84, 4 January 1674), which is the poem in the Rutgers chain. See RESEARCH/DOSSIER_HERT_STERCKTE_I_II.md.
The date EVIDENCE_HOLD is narrowed to the literal reading of the 1676 impression only; inspect printed p. 84 before lifting it.
Recover the exact Russian lyric revision and both verbatim SUNO style prompts.
Re-read actual output metadata before relying on earlier tag notes.
works.tuneDirection: No independent melody: the 1676 print points the singer to I. Hert-sterckte on p. 78 ('Te singen als boven pag.78'), whose own heading names 'Onherroepelijke Jeugd' or 'Gavotte. A la fronté'. Neither tune is acquired; the modern recorded setting is not these tunes.

versions.promptText: slow sacred acoustic hymn, 3/4, 65 bpm, minor mode, warm close-miked male baritone lead with low vibrato and natural diction, restrained chamber ensemble: gut-string cello pedal tones, arco contrabass, theorbo on cadences, small pipe organ pad, one low wooden flute line in verse 5, two-voice choir entering at verse 4 and opening to four parts only in verse 7, unhurried and intimate, quiet dynamics, natural room reverb, no percussion

promptFields.exclude: drums, drum kit, electric bass, synth pad, EDM, cinematic string swell, belting, harsh bass voice, tremolo organ, auto-tune artefacts
promptFields.sections: [Intro — cello and organ pad, 4 bars] / [Verse 1] / [Verse 2] / [Instrumental — theorbo cadence, 2 bars] / [Verse 3] / [Verse 4] / [Verse 5] / [Verse 6] / [Verse 7] / [Outro — voices only on the final line, then silence]
promptFields.repetition: In verse 5, repeat 'Отторгнут от груди — он может' once; in verse 7, repeat 'Ждите ещё Его даров' once

versions.promptSource: Authored in this repository on 2026-10-25 (SUNO/DUTCH-004_PRODUCTION_PACKAGE.md §6). Never submitted to SUNO; not a recovered historical prompt. Distinct from DUTCH-001/002/003, whose submitted prompts are NOT_CAPTURED.
versions.lyricRevisionNote: Russian adaptation, not a translation; owner poetic revision is a required gate before READY_FOR_REVIEW. Deviations disclosed in the production package §4.

works.textChainNote: The poem is a poetic expansion of Psalm 131, first published in 1676; its date of writing is unknown and no date line is printed in either the 1676 or the 1727 edition. The historical melody is unattested, so any recording of this work is a modern setting.
works.rightsNote: The 1676 poem is a public-domain historical work and may be adapted. The 2005 critical edition, the 1971 anthology and the DBNL transcription/images are separate modern objects and must not be reproduced.
